claims.claim: Coherent sits in the AI infrastructure chain at the optical-connectivity layer, where bandwidth and power constraints can force more optical content as clusters scale.
The thesis is not simply AI growth: it requires optical adoption, Coherent share/content retention, successful capacity ramps and economics that survive competitive pricing.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Photonics exposure addresses a scaling bottleneck as AI clusters require higher-bandwidth interconnects.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Optical intensity can rise under several AI scaling paths, but copper persistence, architecture changes or share loss weaken company capture.

factors.name: substitutionResilience
factors.basis: Optics has structural bandwidth advantages at scale, while alternate optical suppliers and architecture choices remain substitutes.

risks.risk: Capacity can become a successor bottleneck if ramps lag demand, or stranded capital if optical demand/share disappoints.

causalEdges.mechanism: larger clusters increase interconnect throughput and energy constraints
causalEdges.falsifier: cluster scaling no longer increases optical requirements

causalEdges.mechanism: optical links can move bandwidth efficiently over required distances
causalEdges.falsifier: copper or alternate architectures remain economically dominant

causalEdges.mechanism: customer adoption converts to component demand if Coherent retains qualified content
causalEdges.falsifier: Coherent loses sockets/share despite industry optical growth

unknowns.unknown: Exact customer concentration and optical content per AI system remain unquantified.

claims.claim: Strong revenue, margin and EPS progression does not currently falsify execution, but exceptional-demand language and capacity expansion increase the cost of an optical-demand or share miss.
The reviewed evidence does not establish durable pricing power, customer diversification, or financing/governance risk; those remain unknown rather than negative findings.

factors.name: thesisQuality
factors.basis: Structural optical demand is plausible and operating execution is strong, but share/content and concentration are not quantified.

factors.name: pricingPower
factors.basis: Margin expansion alone does not prove durable component-level pricing power.

risks.risk: Capacity expansion ahead of realized demand can depress returns and margins.
Competing optical suppliers or customer redesigns can capture industry growth without Coherent retaining proportional economics.
Exceptional demand creates elevated comparison and execution expectations for fiscal 2027.

causalEdges.mechanism: industry optical growth can coexist with weaker company economics
causalEdges.falsifier: Coherent sustains share and margins through competitive capacity additions

unknowns.unknown: Customer concentration and contractual duration are not quantified in reviewed evidence.
No source-addressed current dilution, leverage or governance challenge is established in reviewed Beta inputs.
